Neural dynamical systems, built from parts.

Compose reservoirs, state space models and ODE-based networks as plain nn.Sequential models. Fit the readout in closed form, learn online, or train everything by backprop.

Read out your first reservoir Install

pip install torchdyno

One model, four levels.

There is no model zoo. An echo state network is a cell, two matrices and a linear readout, and every other model is another arrangement of the same parts. 

esn = nn.Sequential(
    Recurrent(LeakyCell(sequence
        input=Dense(3, 300, init=uniform(1.0)),matrices
        recurrent=Dense(300, 300,matrices
            init=spectral(uniform(1.0), 0.9)),
        leak=0.5,
    )).requires_grad_(False),
    nn.Linear(300, 3),readout
)
Ridge(l2=[1e-8, 1e-6]).fit(esn, train, val)learners
evaluate(esn, test, NRMSE())objectives
  1. Matrices

    How a weight matrix is structured, initialised and applied: dense, diagonal, block-diagonal, skew-symmetric or complex.

  2. Sequence

    How a sequence is processed: a recurrent cell run step by step or by a parallel scan, or random convolutions.

  3. Readout

    Pooling over time, then a linear map to the outputs.

  4. Objectives

    The task a model is fitted for, and the metrics it is scored by.

Fit it, or train it.

Fitted, without gradients

Freeze the dynamics and fit the readout: ridge regression in closed form, recursive least squares or FORCE online, with intrinsic plasticity to adapt the reservoir first. A fit takes seconds.

Learners

Trained end to end

Backprop trains every parameter that requires a gradient. Freeze any part with requires_grad_(False) and train the rest around it.

Compared on the same seeds

Run one model three ways, readout only, frozen and fully trained, and report each across seeds.
